\ Description of IPAC file format: http://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/ddgen/ipac_tbl.html
\
\ Astropy Python tool to read IPAC format: http://docs.astropy.org/en/stable/api/astropy.io.ascii.Ipac.html
\
\ IDL tool to read IPAC format: https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/tools/pro/read_ipac_table.pro
\
\ The accompanying documentation for this file is: KSCI-19114
\
\ Column Definitions
\
\ TCE_ID
\     The Threshold Crossing Event (TCE) identifier, consisting of the Kepler Input Catalog (KIC) ID, followed by a dash, and then the planet number
\ KIC
\     The KIC ID of the TCE.
\ Disp
\     The Robovetter Disposition Value (PC or FP)
\ Score
\     The Robovetter Disposition Score
\ NTL
\     The Robovetter Not Transit-Like Flag
\ SS
\     The Robovetter Stellar Eclipse Flag
\ CO
\     The Robovetter Centroid Offset Flag
\ EM
\     The Robovetter Ephemeris Match Flag
\ period
\     The period of the TCE in days from DV
\ epoch
\     The epoch of the TCE in Barycentric Kepler Julian Date (BKJD)
\ Expected_MES
\     The expected value for the Multiple Event Statistic (MES) based on the injection parameters. (Note this value only exists for INJ1, INJ2, and INJ3, and is "null" for OBS, INV, and SCR1.)
\ MES
\     The Multiple Event Statistic (MES) of the TCE
\ NTran
\     The number of transits identified by TPS with SES != 0 (i.e., those used in calculating the MES.)
\ depth
\     The depth of the TCE in parts per million (ppm)
\ duration
\     The duration of the TCE in hours (hrs)
\ Rp
\     The modeled radius of the planet in units of Earth radii (R_earth)
\ Rs
\     The assumed size of the target star in solar radii (R_sun)
\ Ts
\     The assumed temperatue of the target star in Kelvin (K)
\ logg
\     The assumed surface gravity of the star in cm/s**2 (cgs)
\ a
\     The modeled semi-major axis of the orbit in Astronomical Units (AU)
\ Rp/Rs
\     The modeled ratio of the planet radius to stellar radius
\ a/Rs
\     The modeled ratio of the semi-major axis to the stellar radius
\ impact
\     The modeled impact parameter
\ SNR_DV
\     The modeled Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the signal
\ Sp
\     The modeled insolation flux of the planet in units of Earth's insolation flux (S_earth)
\ Fit_Prov
\     A flag indicating if the fit information comes from supplemental fits (1) or original fits (0)
